page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with 1 thread per core, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external network storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core CPU and single-threaded gzip compression tests, which fall into the bottom 25%. However, multi-core and parallelized execution scales to average levels. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Passmark CPU score all rank in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is also average, with cached small-block reads reaching 585.03 GB/sec and uncached large-block writes at 42.85 GB/sec.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is designed for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from multi-threaded scaling rather than raw single-core speed. It is suitable for web serving, with static web serving throughput measured at 9.0 GB/sec, and database operations, achieving 10.16 million Redis SET operations per second. Qualitatively, the lack of bundled local storage and moderate network baseline positions this instance as a cost-efficient option for distributed compute clusters, batch processing, and application servers where persistent storage is decoupled.
